newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO condemns Hamas over its warning to Arafat.
newsitem.headline: PLO condemns Hamas over its warning to Arafat.

text.p: The PLO on Monday denounced remarks by a Hamas spokesman warning Palestinian President Yasser Arafat against cracking down on the militant Islamic group.
Hamas spokesman Ibrahim Ghoshe said earlier in Jordan that Arafat should not heed Israeli demands for a crackdown on its supporters, saying this would unleash deep Palestinian anger.
"It would be dangerous, not just for him (Arafat)...It would lead to Palestinians fighting Palestinians," Ghoshe said.

Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, general secretary in Arafat's office, said in a statement: "Ghoshe's statements are full of hatred and vile and conspiratory and serve the plots of the Israeli right wing, which seeks to destroy the peace process and ignite sedition among our people.

"The Palestinian National Authority is concerned with maintaining national unity and the rule of law and it will not allow Ghoshe or the likes of him to play with the fate of our people or harm the Authority or threaten it with terrorism or civil war."

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has demanded that Arafat crush militant opponents of his interim peace deal as a precondition to resuming negotiations after a double suicide bombing in Jerusalem.
Netanyahu said on Sunday there was a "growing indication" that Hamas was behind the July 30 attack which killed 14 people as well as the bombers.

Arafat has argued that the bombers probably came from abroad, in a defence against sanctions imposed by Israel on Palestinian areas after the bombing and charges from Netanyahu that he has failed to crack down on Moslem militants.
Ghoshe declined to comment on who carried out the attack but said Arafat, who responded to similar bombings last year with a wave of arrests, was in no position to get tough this time.

He said Palestinians were embittered that they had gained little from their 1993 interim self-rule deal with Israel, which Hamas opposes, and were losing faith in the Palestinian Authority after reports of rampant corruption.

"The behaviour of the Palestinian people will not be the same as it was one and a half years ago," said Ghoshe, spokesman for Hamas's exiled leadership. "The Palestinian community is angry with the Palestinian Authority for many reasons."
Ghoshe said Arafat had been given a list of 30 names of people Israel wanted handed over and a further 150 it wanted arrested. He did not say where his information came from.
Arafat has responded to Netanyahu's demands by calling for a lifting of Israel's closure of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, which he said amounted to "state terrorism".

U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross has been holding separate talks with Netanyahu and Arafat to try to bridge their differences, but has said his efforts were focused primarily on addressing Israel's call for security cooperation.
